candidate.title: Seq-Well
candidate.scope: The cell-first Seq-Well workflow in the middle row of the assigned Illumina poster crop: PDMS-well cell capture, co-confinement with barcoded oligo beads under a semi-permeable membrane, lysis and polyA RNA capture, bead recovery, and a barcoded cDNA library. The row is resolved against the original Gierahn et al. 2017 Seq-Well paper at schematic scope. The top Act-Seq and bottom Microwell-seq rows are neighboring context, not target alternatives or branches. This depiction does not assert that every Seq-Well implementation uses the displayed loading order.

states.label: Cell suspension containing single cells with polyadenylated RNA
features: Biological target: cellular polyA RNA; the cell-to-polyA-RNA icon identifies the analyte rather than depicting prior bulk RNA extraction.
The RNA tail is labeled AA(A)n; no chemical end modification is specified.

evidence.locator: Seq-Well row, left: Single cell and polyA RNA with AA(A)n tail; Cell suspension above PDMS subnanoliter array

states.label: Individual intact cells trapped in PDMS subnanoliter wells
features: Cells remain physically separated by array wells; the enlarged well is a detail of the array, not a second branch.
This is the depicted cell-first loading route.

states.label: Oligobeads bearing barcoded poly(dT) capture oligonucleotides
features: Bead-bound oligos contain oligo(dT), a molecular index/UMI, a cell label/barcode, and a universal primer region.
Oligos on a given bead share a cell barcode and carry diverse UMIs; the cartoon does not establish collision-free molecular labeling.
The physical oligo attachment is to the bead; the figure supplies no terminal chemistry or nucleotide sequence.

features: RNA is retained through polyA/poly(dT) hybridization to the oligos on a bead.

states.label: Recovered bead-associated captured mRNA for bulk processing
features: Membrane removal and bead collection end well confinement while retaining captured RNA on its barcoded bead oligos.
The primary paper establishes a bulk-processing interface after bead recovery; the magnet icon and tagged-RNA cartoon alone do not specify cleavage of RNA from beads.

states.label: Barcoded cDNA sequencing library
features: Sequenced carrier: DNA derived by reverse transcription of captured cellular mRNA, with cell barcode and UMI information associated with transcript-derived sequence.
The library represents polyA RNA expression per captured cell through its bead barcode and supports molecule-aware counting through UMIs.
The primary paper identifies paired-end sequencing and Illumina Read 1 sequencing of barcode and UMI; the assigned schematic ends at the library and gives no read lengths or exact read layout.
Membrane confinement reduces cross-contamination; neither the diagram nor that function establishes perfect single-cell purity or complete transcript capture.

operations.label: Individual cells trapped in PDMS nanoarray wells
operations.description: Load the cell suspension into the PDMS array so individual intact cells occupy physically separated subnanoliter wells. The cell-to-polyA-RNA icon identifies what will be measured; it is not an RNA-extraction step before loading.
operations.mechanism: Physical confinement in the PDMS subnanoliter array.
operations.information_effect: Establishes the cell compartment that will associate transcripts with a bead; it does not yet create a molecular barcode on a transcript.

operations.label: Wells are sealed with a semi-permeable membrane
operations.description: Introduce oligobeads into the cell-containing wells, as shown by the plus sign and arrow, and cover the array with a semi-permeable membrane. The output is a co-confined cell-and-bead population in separate sealed wells.
operations.mechanism: The semi-permeable membrane permits solution exchange while retaining biological macromolecules within wells.
operations.information_effect: Keeps the cellular source and its capture bead locally associated during lysis and transcript capture.

operations.label: Cell lysis
operations.description: Disrupt cells inside the sealed wells, releasing their RNAs into the local well contents while capture beads remain present. The figure combines this release and the resulting bead capture in one illustrated transition.
operations.mechanism: Cell lysis in membrane-sealed wells; the membrane allows solution exchange and retains macromolecules.
operations.information_effect: Transfers the target from intracellular RNA to released RNA while preserving compartment-based cell association.

operations.label: PolyA RNA captured by oligobeads
operations.description: Hybridize released polyadenylated mRNAs to poly(dT) oligos attached to the bead in the same well. The output differs from free lysate by RNA attachment through hybridization to a barcoded capture bead.
operations.mechanism: Hybridization of mRNA polyA tails to bead-bound poly(dT).
operations.information_effect: Links captured transcripts physically to a shared bead cell barcode and oligo-specific UMI before their incorporation into cDNA. Capture selects polyadenylated RNA and need not recover all such molecules.

operations.label: Captured mRNA prepared for sequencing — bead recovery
operations.description: Recover the RNA-bearing capture beads from the array, represented by the magnet and rightward arrow. The primary paper resolves the compartment transition: peel off the membrane and remove beads for bulk processing. The detached oligo/RNA cartoons summarize captured material rather than establishing an RNA-release reaction.
operations.mechanism: Membrane removal and recovery of beads carrying captured mRNA.
operations.information_effect: Physical well separation ends, but the bead-oligo barcode association provides the route for retaining cell identity during bulk processing.

[b00011], MAIN: recovery and library-preparation interface

operations.label: Captured mRNA prepared for sequencing → Barcoded cDNA library
operations.description: Convert the recovered captured mRNA into a barcoded cDNA library. Keep this as the broad library-preparation block depicted; the primary paper identifies bulk reverse transcription, amplification and library preparation at this interface.
operations.mechanism: Reverse transcription of captured mRNA, followed by amplification and sequencing-library preparation; internal reactions are not decomposed by this schematic.
operations.information_effect: The DNA library couples transcript-derived sequence to cell barcode and UMI information. Sequencing can assign captured transcript signals to bead-defined cells and use UMIs for molecule-aware counts; it does not directly sequence the native RNA. The paper reports paired-end sequencing with barcode/UMI sequencing in Read 1.

method_scopes.rationale: The assigned card title and middle-row heading both name Seq-Well. Its complete horizontal route is the target. The Gierahn et al. paper specifically supports the PDMS array, poly(dT) barcode beads, semi-permeable membrane, capture and recovered-bead bulk library interface. Lysis and capture are distinguished as successive material transformations supported by the paper within the diagram’s single transition. The shared recovery/preparation caption is retained on two successive operations. Neighboring methods have their own row headings and no connecting arrows; neither is an explicitly depicted Seq-Well alternative.
